messages:
morgan: quick check — after the int4 + new fused-kernel run, how many H100s should we plan for Dedicated for steady 1k rps across eu-west? p99 target 250ms. seeing weird tail spikes in canary.

jia: rough numbers from the bench: with int4+fused we got ~3.6x token/s vs fp16, median latency improved but p99 still depends on concurrency. for 70B chat workload (average seq 120 tokens) one H100 can sustain ~45 concurrent streams to hit 250ms p99 under our batching profile. so for 1k rps that's ~22 gpus (ballpark). :thinking_face:

sasha: re: tail spikes — are these during prefix cache misses? canary logs show KV cache warmup around 40–60ms spikes for cold sessions.

bench-bot: bench summary attached: throughput.csv -> median_tokens_per_sec: 6200, fp16_baseline: 1720, int4_fused: 6210, p50_ms: 65, p95_ms: 180, p99_ms: 320 (concurrency=45)

arash: 320ms p99 is above SLO. we should aim for capacity that keeps p99 <250. either reduce concurrency target per GPU (~35) or add headroom. 35 conc => p99 ~ 220, throughput per GPU drops ~20%. so with 1k rps need ~27 GPUs with 20% autoscale headroom -> plan 34 reserved.

kai: ops note — Dedicated autoscaler currently scales based on GPU_util and queue_length. we saw oscillations when adding small pods. suggest adding a 30% smooth window and burst pool of 6 extra gpus for short surges.

morgan: cool. what's the rollback/upgrade plan for switching kernels in prod? don't want a global perf regression.

deploy-bot: deploy 2361248000 applied to canary (5% traffic). Canary -> metrics: cpu ok, p99 up to 360ms for ~10min then back to 310ms.

sasha: looks like canary experienced memory hiccup leading to small GC-ish pauses in runtime; logs show a kernel fallback on 2 of 8 nodes. kernel selection logic fell back to generic matmul for certain seq lengths.

jia: action items: 1) widen canary to 10% but pin 2 nodes to use legacy kernel to compare. 2) run a warmup sweep that seeds KV cache for synthetic traffic before measuring. 3) re-run concurrency sweep (25,30,35,45) and capture p50/p95/p99.

arash: i'll run the concurrency sweep in eu-west and us-west to verify interregion perf delta. initial calcs show eu-west 7% slower median due to host networking and a different driver version on a subset of hosts.

ops-oncall: ops will hold 6-gpu burst pool (hot spare) for 72hrs after kernel rollout. put a runbook step: if p99>300ms for >5min, trigger fallback to fp16 kernel via rollout flag.

morgan: thanks. last q: for cost estimates, if we reserve 34 + 6 burst = 40 H100s, what's commit delta vs current? finance will need that for quote.
kai: i'll surface exact monthly delta in growth sheet, but rough: +40 H100 = ~+$72k/mo at current committed rates (will confirm).

morgan: perfect. let's reconvene after the region sweep results. thx everyone :thumbsup:
